title: Shared Mutable State as Duplication Prevention
damaged_code:
```rust
static mut GLOBAL_FORMATTER: Option<Formatter> = None; // Shared mutable static to "avoid duplicating" instances
```
pattern: Sharing a single global mutable instance of a utility class (like a cache or formatter) across multiple threads/modules solely to avoid "duplicating" instances.
why_bad: It creates subtle temporal coupling and data races. Trying to avoid memory allocation or instance duplication introduces severe thread synchronization issues and unsafe blocks.
detection: The use of `static mut` global variables or unsynchronized singletons to share state across distinct system components.
counterexample: Explicitly synchronized read-only thread pools or thread-local storage caches.
source: *The Pragmatic Programmer* (20th Anniversary Edition), Topic 34: "Shared State Is Incorrect State", p. 267, 251.
